I dunno. I think the suggestion for a $20 price cut on a $40 game for having a damaged label is absurd. Maybe a $5 discount and only if the damage is substantial. The retro games market isn't exempt from the laws of supply and demand. The supply of original retro games is small and fixed. The demand is what it is. Given that Gamestop is in the unfortunate position of trying to earn a living selling games shipped on a dying medium they aren't going to be jumping at an opportunity to cut their margins.

That having been said, if you can't inspect a used item prior to buying it then it's a little foolhardy to buy it. People will buy anything sight unseen if it's described as new but they wisely insist on more information when it comes to thing that are used. Retro games should be no different.

It just boils down to "How To Be A Savvy Consumer 101". If things like condition, origin, and secondary items (boxes/manuals) are important, then take the time to make sure you're getting what's important and if you can't, then it's a no-sale. Conversely, if you just want an old game for nostalgia's sake, maybe you can afford to be a little less stringent. It shouldn't be about "don't buy from these guys". It should be "if you're thinking of buying, keep this in mind."

It's fine to be cheap, but your rants would carry more weight if you said, "$40 for a used game is too much, charge $20", instead of presenting a lame excuse for a discount. It just flows better when it's genuine and on point.
